This page is the interactive version of the lesson notes (PDF). Each section
has a short summary, a picture, a **Do it** task and one set of questions.
The full explanations, examples, the team activity and the exercises are in
the notes.

## Key terms

{{< glossary game-loop delta-time frame-rate-independence input-vector unit-vector velocity atan2 acceleration damping surface-normal reflection-vector bounciness trs-matrix team-roles >}}

## 27.1 Motion per frame with Δt

- **position += velocity × Δt** in every frame.
- 60 fps: Δt = 1/60 s; the same distance per second at any frame rate.

![The same second at 30 and 60 fps.](images/frame-steps.png){width=94%}

::: {.callout-warning title="Watch out!"}
A fixed step per frame makes the game speed depend on the computer.
:::

::: {.callout-note title="Do it · Δt"}
A meteor at 12 units per second: the step at 30, 60 and 144 fps.
:::

::: {.callout-tip title="Try it 1 · Steps"}
Choose the right answer.

::: {.match extra="12|0.5"}
speed 5, 60 fps: step per frame
:   about 0.083

speed 5, 30 fps: step per frame
:   about 0.167

speed 9, 30 fps: step per frame
:   0.3

30 fps without Δt (step 0.083): distance per second
:   2.5
:::
:::

## 27.2 Input and diagonal movement

- Input (1, 1) has length 1.41: **normalize** it if its length > 1.
- velocity = speed × normalized input.

![Diagonal input.](images/diagonal.png){width=94%}

{{< sim file="sims/move-lab.html" poster="sims/move-lab.png" title="Move Lab: fly the shuttle of Star Dock" height="820" >}}

::: {.callout-warning title="Watch out!"}
Never normalize (0, 0): check the length first.
:::

::: {.callout-note title="Do it · Diagonals"}
In **Move Lab**, fly ↗ with and without "normalize input"; compute speed 8,
input (−1, 1).
:::

::: {.callout-tip title="Try it 2 · Diagonals"}
Use Move Lab. Choose the right answer.

::: {.match extra="10|1"}
speed 5, input (1, 1), not normalized
:   about 7.07

speed 5, input (1, 1), normalized
:   5

(1, −1) normalized
:   (0.71, −0.71)

speed 6, (1, 1) normalized: velocity
:   about (4.24, 4.24)
:::
:::

## 27.3 Facing the velocity

- **θ = atan2(v~y~, v~x~)** for a sprite drawn facing +x.
- Turn only when the speed is not 0.

![Face the velocity.](images/facing.png){width=94%}

::: {.callout-warning title="Watch out!"}
atan2(y, x), not atan2(x, y).
:::

::: {.callout-note title="Do it · Facing"}
The facing angle for (5, 5), (−4, 3) and (0, −2).
:::

::: {.callout-tip title="Try it 3 · Angles"}
Choose the facing angle.

::: {.match extra="45°|0°"}
v = (3, 4)
:   about 53.1°

v = (−5, 0)
:   180°

v = (−1, 1)
:   135°

v = (0, −3)
:   −90°
:::
:::

## 27.4 Acceleration and damping

- **v += a × Δt** up to the max speed.
- Released: **v ×= 1 − k × Δt** in every frame.

![Speed over time.](images/accel.png){width=94%}

::: {.callout-warning title="Watch out!"}
Damping without Δt depends on the frame rate.
:::

::: {.callout-note title="Do it · Smooth flight"}
In **Move Lab**, accelerate and face the velocity, then let go. a = 8, max
6: when is the max reached?
:::

::: {.callout-tip title="Try it 4 · Smooth flight"}
Choose the right answer.

::: {.match extra="5 s|1"}
a = 10, max 5: time to max
:   0.5 s

a = 8, max 6: time to max
:   0.75 s

k = 4, 60 fps: factor per frame
:   about 0.933

k = 6, 60 fps: factor per frame
:   0.9
:::
:::

## 27.5 Bouncing off walls

- **v' = v − 2(v · n)n**, n the unit normal of the wall.
- Bounciness e: **v' = v − (1 + e)(v · n)n**.

![A bounce.](images/bounce.png){width=94%}

{{< sim file="sims/bounce-lab.html" poster="sims/bounce-lab.png" title="Bounce Lab: reflect the velocity" height="680" >}}

::: {.callout-warning title="Watch out!"}
Only the part along the normal changes its sign.
:::

::: {.callout-note title="Do it · Bounces"}
Check Example 27.5 in **Bounce Lab**; reflect (−2, 5) on the ceiling
n = (0, −1).
:::

::: {.callout-tip title="Try it 5 · Bounces"}
Use Bounce Lab. Choose the right answer.

::: {.match extra="(−4, −3)|(3, 4)"}
(4, −3) on the floor, e = 1
:   (4, 3)

(4, −3) on the floor, e = 0.8
:   (4, 2.4)

(4, 3) on the right wall, e = 1
:   (−4, 3)

(3, −2) on the floor, e = 1
:   (3, 2)
:::
:::

## 27.6 Drawing the sprite: local to world

- World corner = **T · R · S · local corner**: scale, rotate, then move.
- One 3 × 3 matrix in homogeneous coordinates.

![Local corners to world.](images/sprite-trs.png){width=94%}

::: {.callout-warning title="Watch out!"}
Translate last, or the sprite circles around the origin.
:::

::: {.callout-note title="Do it · World corners"}
Scale 1, angle 180°, position (2, 4): the three world corners.
:::

::: {.callout-tip title="Try it 6 · World corners"}
Scale 2, angle 90°, position (5, 3). Choose the world point.

::: {.match extra="(7, 3)|(2, 0)"}
nose (1, 0)
:   (5, 5)

back (−0.5, 0.5)
:   (4, 2)

back (−0.5, −0.5)
:   (6, 2)

the local origin (0, 0)
:   (5, 3)
:::
:::

## Game challenge: Pilot Check {.challenge}

Work alone. Use every section of today.

Six checks: the **step at 30 fps**, a **diagonal**, the **facing angle**,
the **time to max speed**, a **bounce** and the **sprite's nose**.

{{< sim file="sims/pilot-check.html" poster="sims/pilot-check.png" title="Pilot Check: six numbers of the movement code" kind="game" height="440" >}}

::: {.callout-tip title="Try it 7 · The checks"}
Choose the right answer.

::: {.match extra="0.083|(−4, 3)"}
the step at 30 fps, speed 5
:   about 0.167

the diagonal speed without normalizing
:   about 7.07

the bounce of (4, −3) on the floor
:   (4, 3)

the time to max speed 5 with a = 10
:   0.5 s
:::
:::

::: {.callout-tip title="Try it 8 · Compute (harder)"}
Choose the right answer.

::: {.match extra="(−5, −1)|(3, −2)"}
reflect (−5, 1) on the left wall n = (1, 0)
:   (5, 1)

(3, −2) on the floor with e = 0.5
:   (3, 1)

nose (1, 0), scale 1, 90°, position (3, 3)
:   (3, 4)

the facing angle of (−3, −4)
:   about −126.9°
:::
:::

## Summary {.summary}

- position += velocity × Δt: the same speed at every frame rate.
- Normalize the input so diagonals are not faster.
- Face the velocity with atan2(v~y~, v~x~).
- Accelerate with a × Δt; damp with 1 − k × Δt.
- Bounce: v' = v − (1 + e)(v · n)n.
- Draw the sprite with T · R · S.
